turns.text: Certainly! Let's say there’s a student who believes they only need to focus on the theoretical aspects of the experiment and doesn’t see the value in practical execution. The teacher could start by having the student observe a peer who excels at both theory and practice, noting what makes that approach effective. Then, the teacher might encourage the student to participate more actively in hands-on activities, perhaps by assigning them roles that require both theoretical understanding and practical application. This way, the student can see firsthand how both aspects complement each other and build confidence in their ability to integrate them.
